newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT - Dlr regroups for renewed attack on top.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dlr regroups for renewed attack on top.

text.p: The dollar, after a retreat that demonstrated little conviction on the part of the sellers, is ready to regroup and march on several key resistance levels, analysts said on Wednesday.,
Dollar/mark briefly tested strong support at 1.7850 only to quickly claw its way back above 1.79.
This leaves the scope open for a retest of the prior resistance at 1.8025, taken out on Tuesday, and of 1.8040 -- the latest 71-month high set during the same session.
In late trade, dollar/mark was quoted at 1.7930/40 versus 1.7885/95 at the open.
"We may be consolidating over the short term. But we should revisit the high of yesterday," said senior analyst Scott Siller at MCM CurrencyWatch. "The target in this move remains 1.8075/85."
But Siller said the charts pointed to more important gains on dollar/mark in the sessions ahead.
"I see a breakout target in a measured move at 1.8235. Then channel projections from recent high/lows put dollar/mark in the 1.8430/1.8550 area," Siller added.
The 1.8550-mark level would be the objective in an upside projection drawn from the mid-November and mid-March lows.
Chartists noted that different studies projected the recent dollar/mark moves above the 1.8430 high of July 1991 -- itself a high since 1989.
Meanwhile, dollar/yen was quoted at 115.30/35 versus 115.65/75 at the open.
"Dollar/yen looks very good," Siller said, predicting that "there should not be much in the way to 117.0, the 38-percent retracement from the May 1 high (at 127.46) to the June 11 low (at 110.62)."
"The dollar/yen daily studies are positive and it's not overbought," Siller added.

Chartists said mark/yen was improving but still shy of 65.55, previously a key support and now a major resistance, while sterling/mark is consolidating after a breath-taking run. It remains bullish unless key support at 3.0025 gives way.
Dollar/Swiss mirrored dollar/mark and is positioned to recapture 1.48 -- a big level briefly breached on Tuesday.
Analysts said such dollar/Swiss rebound would signal more bullishness for dollar/mark and lead to the retest of 1.4922, the 1997 high.
